note: Chains that publish per-dish nutrition in a form that can be read at source. Every entry here must be VERIFIED by fetching it: an unverified URL costs a wasted fetch and then falls through to the model anyway, and a guessed one that happens to resolve to an aggregator would put label confidence on somebody's estimate. `platform` selects the parser in lib/restaurants.py. UK chain kcal on menus is mandatory, but full macros are not, so most chains publish only via a platform like this one - which is exactly why a plain web search cannot replace this rung.
how_to_add: Find the chain's allergen/nutrition link on its own site (usually in the footer), fetch it, and confirm it serves per-dish macros as static HTML rather than a JavaScript app. Then add the vendor with that URL and its platform. Verify with: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'ClaudeCoach/lib'); import restaurants as R; m=R.load_menu('<key>', R.load_registry()['<key>'], '/tmp/rcache'); print(len(m['rows']), m.get('error'))"

wagamama.notes: Linked from wagamama.com/allergen-information. The chain's own menu pages are JavaScript-rendered and yield nothing to a fetch. Northern Ireland has a separate matrix (…allergymatrix03) not wired here.

swap_groups.note: A rice bowl is published with sticky rice. Ordering brown rice instead is a SWAP, not an addition, so the difference between the two published side rows is the honest adjustment - and it is mostly fibre (+3.5 g), not energy (-8 kcal). Nothing in the order line marks it as a change, which is why it needs naming here: 'with brown rice' reads like part of the dish.
